title: 2010 AMC 12A Problem 3
statement: Rectangle \(ABCD,\) pictured below, shares \(50\%\) of its area with square \(EFGH.\) Square \(EFGH\) shares \(20\%\) of its area with rectangle \(ABCD.\) What is \(\dfrac{AB}{AD}?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(s\) be the side length of square \(EFGH.\) The shaded overlap has width \(s\) and height \(AD,\) so its area is \(s\cdot AD.\)

Because the overlap is \(50\%\) of the rectangle, \(s\cdot AD=\tfrac12\,AB\cdot AD,\) so \(AB=2s.\) Because it is \(20\%\) of the square, \(s\cdot AD=\tfrac15 s^2,\) so \(AD=\tfrac{s}{5}.\)

Therefore \[\dfrac{AB}{AD}=\dfrac{2s}{\frac{s}{5}}=10.\]

Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: Let \(s\) be the side length of the square; the shaded overlap has width \(s\) and height \(AD\)
Half the rectangle’s area equals the overlap, giving \(AB=2s;\) one fifth of the square’s area gives \(AD=\tfrac{s}{5}\)
